summary.oneLiner: Gini Silk Mills Limited is a Maharashtra-based textile company engaged in fabric manufacturing and processing, which registered a turnover of Rs. 3,904.33 Lakhs in FY 2025-26.
summary.business: Gini Silk Mills Limited participates in India's textile and apparel value chain, with fabric processing forming the bulk of its revenue base. The Company states that its textile product is well accepted by customers and that it is in the process of increasing its customer portfolio. It operates a factory establishment at MIDC Tarapur, Boisar (Thane, Maharashtra), and references an advanced material division that management says continues to grow at a rapid pace.

endMarkets: Domestic Indian textile market|Export markets (global textile and clothing markets; foreign exchange inflow of Rs. 12.71 Lakhs in the current year)

risks.note: Management flags 'Volatility in raw material prices, particularly cotton, silk and man-made fibres' as a threat in the MD&A. As a fabric processor and manufacturer with thin operating margins, input-cost swings pass straight through to profitability.

risks.risk: Intense competition from domestic and international textile manufacturers
risks.note: Listed explicitly among MD&A threats. The Company is a small participant in a fragmented, commoditised value chain and states it is still 'in the process of increasing our customer portfolio', so it has limited pricing power.

risks.risk: Export demand exposed to global economic uncertainty
risks.note: MD&A lists 'Global economic uncertainties affecting export demand' as a threat, and the industry commentary notes exports held up only 'despite continued macroeconomic uncertainties and subdued demand in certain international markets'.

MD&A flags 'Fluctuations in foreign exchange rates impacting export competitiveness and import costs'. Foreign exchange inflow fell sharply year on year (Rs. 12.71 Lakhs current year versus Rs. 217.07 Lakhs previous year, per the forex earnings and outgo disclosure), so the export stream is small and volatile.

risks.risk: Cost inflation in energy, logistics and labour compressing operating margins
risks.note: MD&A names 'Rising energy, logistics and labour costs, which may affect operating margins' as a threat. The disclosed key-ratio movement shows operating and net profit margins and return on net worth all lower in FY 2025-26 than FY 2024-25, so the buffer against further cost inflation is thin.

MD&A flags 'Changes in regulatory policies, environmental compliance requirements and geopolitical developments'. Wet processing and dyeing at the Tarapur MIDC site is an effluent-intensive activity exposed to tightening environmental norms.

risks.risk: Related-party concentration with Gini Tex Private Limited
risks.note: Not labelled a risk by the Company, but structurally material: AOC-2 shows processing job work, purchase of grey/dyed fabrics, sale of dyed fabrics and rent paid to Gini Tex Private Limited, a common-director/common-shareholder entity of the Harlalka family, and the AGM notice seeks approval for FY 2026-27 transactions with that party (plus a promoter loan) expected to exceed 10% of annual turnover. A large slice of the operating chain therefore runs through a promoter-affiliated counterparty rather than the open market.

risks.risk: Single-site, single-activity concentration with no in-house R&D
risks.note: The only manufacturing location referenced is the factory establishment at E-15, MIDC, Tarapur, Boisar, Thane, Maharashtra; the Company reports no Subsidiaries, Associates or Joint Ventures during FY 2025-26; and it states it does not have a separate division for research and development, with no expenditure earmarked for that activity. Revenue is concentrated in fabric processing, so any disruption at the one site or in that one activity is not diversified away.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management flags 'Volatility in raw material prices, particularly cotton, silk and man-made fibres' as a threat in the MD&A. As a fabric processor and manufacturer with thin operating margins, input-cost swings pass straight through to profitability.
- Listed explicitly among MD&A threats. The Company is a small participant in a fragmented, commoditised value chain and states it is still 'in the process of increasing our customer portfolio', so it has limited pricing power.
- MD&A lists 'Global economic uncertainties affecting export demand' as a threat, and the industry commentary notes exports held up only 'despite continued macroeconomic uncertainties and subdued demand in certain international markets'.
- MD&A flags 'Fluctuations in foreign exchange rates impacting export competitiveness and import costs'. Foreign exchange inflow fell sharply year on year (Rs. 12.71 Lakhs current year versus Rs. 217.07 Lakhs previous year, per the forex earnings and outgo disclosure), so the export stream is small and volatile.
- MD&A names 'Rising energy, logistics and labour costs, which may affect operating margins' as a threat. The disclosed key-ratio movement shows operating and net profit margins and return on net worth all lower in FY 2025-26 than FY 2024-25, so the buffer against further cost inflation is thin.
- MD&A flags 'Changes in regulatory policies, environmental compliance requirements and geopolitical developments'. Wet processing and dyeing at the Tarapur MIDC site is an effluent-intensive activity exposed to tightening environmental norms.
- Not labelled a risk by the Company, but structurally material: AOC-2 shows processing job work, purchase of grey/dyed fabrics, sale of dyed fabrics and rent paid to Gini Tex Private Limited, a common-director/common-shareholder entity of the Harlalka family, and the AGM notice seeks approval for FY 2026-27 transactions with that party (plus a promoter loan) expected to exceed 10% of annual turnover. A large slice of the operating chain therefore runs through a promoter-affiliated counterparty rather than the open market.
- The only manufacturing location referenced is the factory establishment at E-15, MIDC, Tarapur, Boisar, Thane, Maharashtra; the Company reports no Subsidiaries, Associates or Joint Ventures during FY 2025-26; and it states it does not have a separate division for research and development, with no expenditure earmarked for that activity. Revenue is concentrated in fabric processing, so any disruption at the one site or in that one activity is not diversified away.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on core strengths product segments within the textile space
- Continue building marketing and distribution footprints with renewed vigour during the coming year
- Increase the customer portfolio in Textiles on the back of product acceptance
- Deliver quality products, improve operational efficiencies and respond to changing market requirements
- Pursue growth in the advanced material division, which management says continues to grow at a rapid pace
